title: Alternating Current and L-C-R Circuits
short_intro: Alternating current refers to an electrical current that reverses direction periodically, typically sinusoidally with time. It is fundamentally characterized by parameters such as root-mean-square value, frequency, and phase relationships across passive circuit elements.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Mean and RMS values of AC, pure resistor, inductor, and capacitor in AC circuits, series LCR resonance, quality factor, and power in AC circuits.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Parallel LCR circuits, parallel resonance conditions, AC bridges, vector diagrams, transient phenomena, and complex impedance phasor representation.

concept_notes.heading: Mean and Root Mean Square (RMS) Values of Alternating Current
bullets: The mean or average value of a sinusoidal alternating current over a complete cycle is zero due to equal positive and negative half-cycles.
The mean value over a half-cycle is given by I<sub>mean</sub> = (2I<sub>0</sub>)/π ≈ 0.637I<sub>0</sub>, where I<sub>0</sub> is the peak current.
The root-mean-square (RMS) or virtual value is defined as the square root of the mean of squared instantaneous values, given by I<sub>rms</sub> = I<sub>0</sub>/&sqrt;2 ≈ 0.707I<sub>0</sub>.

concept_notes.heading: AC through Pure R, L, and C Circuits
bullets: In a pure resistor, alternating voltage and current are in phase, with impedance Z = R.
In a pure inductor of inductance L, the alternating voltage leads the current by a phase angle of π/2 radians, and the inductive reactance is X<sub>L</sub> = ωL.
In a pure capacitor of capacitance C, the alternating current leads the voltage by π/2 radians, and the capacitive reactance is X<sub>C</sub> = 1/(ωC).

concept_notes.heading: Series LCR Circuit and Resonance
bullets: In a series combination of R, L, and C connected to an AC source, the total impedance is Z = √[R<sup>2</sup> + (X<sub>L</sub> - X<sub>C</sub>)<sup>2</sup>].
Resonance occurs when the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance (X<sub>L</sub> = X<sub>C</sub>), minimizing impedance to Z = R.
The resonant angular frequency is given by ω<sub>0</sub> = 1/√(LC), at which the current is maximum and in phase with the applied voltage.

concept_notes.heading: Quality Factor (Q-factor) and Power in AC Circuits
bullets: The Quality factor (Q-factor) measures the sharpness of resonance, defined as the ratio of voltage across L or C to the applied voltage at resonance: Q = (ω<sub>0</sub>L)/R.
The true power dissipated in an AC circuit is given by P<sub>avg</sub> = V<sub>rms</sub> I<sub>rms</sub> cos φ, where cos φ is the power factor.
Power factor can be improved by connecting a suitable capacitor in parallel with inductive loads.

derivations.title: Impedance and Phase Angle of a Series LCR Circuit
derivations.conditions: AC voltage source v = V<sub>0</sub> sin(ωt) connected in series with R, L, and C.
steps: Write the voltage equations across each component: V<sub>R</sub> = I R (in phase with I), V<sub>L</sub> = I X<sub>L</sub> (leads I by 90°), V<sub>C</sub> = I X<sub>C</sub> (lags I by 90°).

Use phasor addition for the total voltage: V<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> = V<sub>R</sub><sup>2</sup> + (V<sub>L</sub> - V<sub>C</sub>)<sup>2</sup> = (I<sub>0</sub>R)<sup>2</sup> + (I<sub>0</sub>X<sub>L</sub> - I<sub>0</sub>X<sub>C</sub>)<sup>2</sup>.
Factor out I<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> to express total impedance Z = V<sub>0</sub> / I<sub>0</sub> = √[R<sup>2</sup> + (X<sub>L</sub> - X<sub>C</sub>)<sup>2</sup>].
Determine the phase angle φ between voltage and current using tan φ = (X<sub>L</sub> - X<sub>C</sub>) / R.

derivations.title: Resonant Frequency and Bandwidth of Series LCR Circuit
derivations.conditions: Series LCR circuit driven at varying frequencies with constant voltage amplitude.
steps: Condition for resonance is when reactive terms cancel out: X<sub>L</sub> = X<sub>C</sub>.
Define half-power frequencies where current drops to 1/√2 of its maximum value, yielding bandwidth Δω = R / L.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Current vs Frequency Resonance Curve
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Plot of RMS current (I<sub>rms</sub>) on the y-axis against angular frequency (ω) on the x-axis for different values of resistance R.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Shows a sharp peak at ω<sub>0</sub>. Lower resistance yields a sharper peak and higher Q-factor.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Directly tested in conceptual MCQs regarding sharpness of resonance and bandwidth.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Phasor Diagram for Series LCR Circuit
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A vector diagram showing current along the reference axis, V<sub>R</sub> in phase, V<sub>L</sub> leading by 90°, and V<sub>C</sub> lagging by 90°.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Geometric addition of orthogonal voltages to derive total impedance and phase angle φ.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to determine phase relationships and instantaneous voltage equations.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Parallel Resonance Curve (Impedance vs Frequency)
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Plot of Impedance (Z) vs Frequency (f) showing a maximum impedance peak at parallel resonance.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: At parallel resonance, impedance is maximum and current drawn from the source is minimum (rejector circuit).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Differentiating between series (acceptor) and parallel (rejector) resonance circuits in PGT exams.

solved_numericals.question: A 100 Ω resistor is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz AC source. Calculate the RMS value of current and the peak current.
solution_steps: Identify given values: V<sub>rms</sub> = 220 V, R = 100 &Omega.
Calculate RMS current: I<sub>rms</sub> = V<sub>rms</sub> / R = 220 / 100 = 2.2 A.
Calculate peak current: I<sub>0</sub> = I<sub>rms</sub> × √2 = 2.2 × 1.414 = 3.11 A.

solved_numericals.question: An inductor of inductance 0.5 H and a resistor of 200 Ω are connected in series to a 240 V, 50 Hz AC supply. Find the maximum current in the circuit.
solution_steps: Calculate inductive reactance X<sub>L</sub> = 2 π f L = 2 × (22/7) × 50 × 0.5 = 157.1 Ω.
Calculate peak voltage V<sub>0</sub> = V<sub>rms</sub> × √2 = 240 × 1.414 = 339.4 V.
Calculate peak current I<sub>0</sub> = V<sub>0</sub> / Z = 339.4 / 254.3 = 1.33 A.

solved_numericals.question: A series LCR circuit with L = 2.0 H, C = 32 μF, and R = 10 Ω is connected to a 200 V variable frequency AC source. Find (a) the resonant frequency, (b) the Q-factor of the circuit, and (c) the bandwidth.
solution_steps: (a) Resonant angular frequency ω<sub>0</sub> = 1 / √(LC) = 1 / √(2.0 × 32 × 10<sup>-6</sup>) = 1 / √(64 × 10<sup>-6</sup>) = 1 / (8 × 10<sup>-3</sup>) = 125 rad/s. Resonant frequency f<sub>0</sub> = ω<sub>0</sub> / (2π) = 125 / (2 × 3.1416) = 19.89 Hz.

assumptions_and_limitations: Components (R, L, C) are assumed to be ideal, linear, and constant with respect to temperature and frequency unless specified otherwise.
The source EMF is assumed to be purely sinusoidal.
Stray capacitances and lead resistances are neglected in theoretical derivations.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The average power consumed by a pure inductor or pure capacitor in an AC circuit is zero.
common_misconceptions.correct: The average power consumed over a complete cycle by pure L and pure C is indeed zero, but reactive power oscillates between the source and the field.
common_misconceptions.why: The phase angle between voltage and current is 90°, making cos(π/2) = 0.

common_misconceptions.wrong: At resonance in a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the inductor or capacitor is zero.
common_misconceptions.correct: At resonance, the net reactive voltage (V<sub>L</sub> - V<sub>C</sub>) is zero, but individual voltages V<sub>L</sub> and V<sub>C</sub> can be very large depending on the Q-factor.
common_misconceptions.why: V<sub>L</sub> and V<sub>C</sub> are 180° out of phase with each other and cancel out externally, but individually maintain potential drops equal to Q times the supply voltage.

quick_revision: In pure R, voltage and current are in phase; in L, voltage leads current by 90°; in C, current leads voltage by 90°.
Series resonance condition: X<sub>L</sub> = X<sub>C</sub>, Z = R, and current is maximum.
Power factor cos φ = R / Z; true power P = V<sub>rms</sub> I<sub>rms</sub> cos φ.
